subject: Cost & latency decomposition canvas — interactive explainer tiles request
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Acme Data <eng-data@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2029 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Cost & latency decomposition canvas — interactive explainer tiles request

Hi team,

Following a bunch of high-cost alerts last week (Acme reported two spikes during midday traffic), I want to propose a small console addition: an "interactive decomposition canvas" on the route detail page that surfaces the top attribution vectors for a selected anomaly window. The idea is an explainer tile users can click through to see a compact narrative + prioritized investigation starters.

Desired behaviors:
- Single-click breakdown by token-category (prompt vs. generation), model variant, and quantization profile for the selected time window.
- Expandable explanation lines — e.g., "80% of incremental cost came from long completions (avg length +45 tokens) on route /checkout/ai-receipt" with a short suggested mitigator (cap gen-length or route-specific token cap).
- A lightweight drill: "show example traces (3)" that opens a sanitized trace inspector (no PII) and an exported CSV of route-attribution metrics.
- Inline action links: open a canary rollout, add a prefix cache rule, or create an Ops ticket pre-filled with context (route, time window, metric deltas).

Why now: the recurring back-and-forth between Product, Eng, and Customer Success on these anomalies is taking too long. If we give customers (and our CS/SE teams) a compact, standardized starting point, we reduce triage time and inconsistent suggested mitigations.

Ask: can Eng + Analytics scope an MVP for the canvas (data transform and API contract) and Jasmine/Design scope two small mockups? Suggested scope: 3 panels (summary narrative, top-3 attribution lines, example traces) and two action links. Timebox: 2 sprints to prototype.

Attached: short screenshot of an Acme spike (anonymized), a draft UX mockup, and the SQL I used to pull the initial attribution metrics.

Next steps: quick sync Wed 10am PT? If that works I can invite the Acme eng lead for context.

Thanks,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Product Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Acme Data <eng-data@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2029 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cost & latency decomposition canvas — interactive explainer tiles request

Thanks Sofia — strong idea. Quick notes from Analytics side:

- We can produce the per-route token-category split and model-variant deltas from the event store and the token ingestion pipeline; rough estimate ~6 hours to wire a query and 1 day to validate sampling bias.
- Example traces: we should cap to 3-5 per window and redact any user text. We already have sanitized trace exports for CS.
- Caveat: short windows (<=5 min) often have noisy attribution due to batching effects — we should default to a minimum 15-minute aggregation window in the UI.

I've attached the cleaned SQL I used and a quick CSV sample with the attribution columns (route, window_start, delta_cost_pct, avg_tokens_prompt, avg_tokens_gen, model_variant, quant_profile). I also pushed a small schema change proposal to OBS-431 for the attribution fields.

I'll block time to join Wed 10am PT.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Applied ML / Analytics
Redwood Inference

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 May 2029 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cost & latency decomposition canvas — interactive explainer tiles request

On Tue, May 21, 2029 at 09:04 AM Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Sofia — strong idea. Quick notes from Analytics side:
>
> - We can produce the per-route token-category split and model-variant deltas from the event store and the token ingestion pipeline; rough estimate ~6 hours to wire a query and 1 day to validate sampling bias.

Love this. A couple UX constraints / proposals:
- Keep the top-level tile to 3 lines (summary sentence + 2 bullets) so the route page doesn't become noisy. Expand to full canvas only when the user clicks "Explain anomaly".
- For the narrative line, use templated sentences with variable placeholders so we can A/B iterate phrasing without rework (e.g., "X% of incremental cost was driven by Y on route Z — likely cause: Q").
- Action links should open a modal with contextual defaults rather than jump-to-other-page. That keeps the user in flow.

I'll put two small mocks in the Notion link and add annotations on interaction states. Also — quick UI question: do we want the "sanitized example traces" to open a read-only inspector or an inline preview? My vote: inspector modal with a link to download CSV.

-Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Design Lead, Developer Experience
Redwood Inference

https://notion.so/r/Route-Anomaly-Canvas-5f9d

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Acme Data <eng-data@acme.com>, Bethany Rosen <bethany.rosen@bigretail.com>
Date: Wed, 22 May 2029 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cost & latency decomposition canvas — interactive explainer tiles request

+1 from Ops. Implementation notes:
- Instrumentation gap: we currently do not record quant_profile consistently for older model variants in the 2028-09 images. Analytics will need to backfill or we default to "unknown" in the canvas. Backfill ETA depends on storage retention (I can scope).
- Canary actions: Ops prefers a pre-filled runbook link rather than direct rollout triggers for customer-facing consoles. We'll provide an endpoint that returns a pre-populated runbook JSON.
- Security: make sure example traces for external accounts are double-redacted and accessioned. I'll coordinate with Security on the export flow.

Action items agreed for Wed sync:
1) Analytics (Marcus) — confirm sample query and share perf/load implications (before sync).
2) Design (Jasmine) — paste two mocks in Notion and a compact interaction spec.
3) Eng (Dylan + Irene) — draft API contract for the canvas (data fields, redaction rules, action link payloads).
4) PM (Sofia) — invite Acme eng lead and CS rep to the sync.

I'll add these to OBS-431. See you at 10am PT.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
SRE / Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference
